Brief: Describe the Great Barrier Reef and the threats it faces. — about Human use

1. The Great Barrier Reef has long been known to and used by the Aboriginal Australian and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
2. Aboriginal Australians have been living in the area for at least 40,000 years, and Torres Strait Islanders since about 10,000 years ago.
3. For these 70 or so clan groups, the reef is also an important cultural feature.
4. In 1768, Louis de Bougainville encountered the reef, but did not explore it.
5. On 11 June 1770, HM Bark Endeavour, captained by explorer James Cook, ran aground on the Great Barrier Reef, sustaining considerable damage.
6. Lightening the ship and re-floating it during an incoming tide eventually saved it.
7. One of the most famous wrecks was HMS Pandora, which sank on 29 August 1791, killing 35 men.
8. The Queensland Museum has led archaeological digs to wreck of Pandora since 1983.
9. Because the reef had no atolls, it was largely unstudied in the 19th century.
10. During this time, some of the reef's islands were mined for deposits of guano, and lighthouses were built as beacons throughout the system. as in Raine Island, the earliest example.
11. In 1922, the Great Barrier Reef Committee began carrying out much of the early research on the reef.
